sense.text:
This is a war in the spirit and in the flesh, and it begins with knowing who God is. “For the Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords”: the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob is the God of all gods. There are many self-proclaimed gods, many inserted gods, all type of gods, but he is God over every one of them. He is also the God of you gods, because we are the gods upon the earth.

“A great God, a mighty, and a terrible”: you can’t go past that part. He is mighty and he is terrible.

“Which regardeth not persons”: when judgment is set, when whatever the Lord has ordained is set, he doesn’t regard whether you are a king or a homeless man in the dust. If the punishment is ordained, that is what it will be. He will not respect your status or your tenure. The judgment is set, the arrow is shot, the dart is thrown, and it is going to its appointed place.

“Nor taketh reward”: you can’t bribe the Lord. Your bank account can be in the millions, billions and trillions, and he doesn’t need your money, your riches, your jewels or stocks in your company. He doesn’t need any of it.

“For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee”: God has surnamed us. “Though thou hast not known me”: the Lord has revealed himself to us and delivered us numerous times, and for some reason we continue to turn our backs on him.
“I am the Lord, and there is none else, there is no God beside me: I girded thee, though thou hast not known me.” The Lord is saying, I have girded you, and you still don’t know me.

“That they may know from the rising of the sun, and from the west, that there is none beside me.” Some insert themselves as gods; some create false gods, both in their mind and as physical idols. The Lord says there is none with him. “I am the Lord, and there is none else.”

“I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil.” The Lord makes peace and the Lord creates evil. “I the Lord do all these things.” This is the beginning of the overall picture of the Lord our God: one God over all, who does all these things.

precepts.why:
“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” The same Lord that forms the light, creates darkness, makes peace and creates evil is also a man of war.

That is the God we serve: the God that formed the light and created darkness, the God of war. And that God of war is Christ.

sense.text: “The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge.” The God of Jacob is our refuge: our protector, our shield, our covering.

“Come, behold the works of the Lord, what desolations he hath made in the earth.” Come and look at the desolations the Lord has made in time past. It shows there is no god with him, because there were many leaders who thought themselves to be God. Pharaohs were worshipped as God. Xerxes thought he was a god. As these leaders rise in power they also rise in pride. Antiochus did the same thing: Antiochus Epiphanes thought himself God manifest on earth. The desolations of the Lord brought every one of them down.

“He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth.” This God is able to make wars cease, from one end of the earth to the other. There is a man on the thumbnail who has been claiming for two years that he is going to stop the war between Ukraine and Russia, and he hasn’t been able to stop anything. The God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob is the one who determines when wars cease.

“He breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder; he burneth the chariot in the fire.” Recently the Iron Dome in Israel failed, and rockets came through. All the things the nations think are their protection, the Lord says, I will make your bow, your weaponry, fail. That failure wasn’t a technical glitch or a technical error. The Lord put his fingers in it and ripped it open like you rip a shirt, and the missiles went right in. He causes the prideful instruments of man to fail, because he determines where war happens and when it ceases.
“Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.” God says he will be exalted among the heathen and in the earth.
“The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge.” The God of Jacob is our refuge.

“Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight.” This is King David speaking about how the Lord enabled him and equipped him with his mighty fighting skills. Our God is our refuge, and our God is a man of war, and he is teaching his soldiers to do the same thing.

We are called as soldiers too. We are in a boot camp, a training camp, and the Lord is teaching us how to war.

Think how it was in the church: someone asked what you learned in church today and you were clueless. You read John 3:16 a billion times before you came into this truth. Then within a year or two you know the breakdown of the scriptures and can give a million scriptures to explain one verse. When did that spirit of discipline switch on, that spirit of understanding? The Lord flipped the switch. He is teaching you how to war, calling you to be a soldier and a servant, and you didn’t even know it. Things you would never have retained before, you retain now. It is boot camp.

precepts.why:
“Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.”

The same God who is a man of war has handpicked every one of us to be soldiers in his mighty army. He chose us to be soldiers, and a soldier doesn’t entangle himself with the affairs of this life. That is why David’s words are ours: the Lord teaches our hands to war too.

Some brothers think they are just here for unleavened bread, just here to be around the brothers. No. Everything going on in the earth, in your household and in the congregation should be a learning lesson, because there are spirits involved in all of those things, and we are being taught and built up to deal with those different spirits.

You start with yourself, then your household, then the streets, then the congregation. If you can’t control, subdue and put in subjection your own body, how will you tell your family to be in subjection, and how will you do it in the congregation? Working on yourself is not a one-step, one-time process; it goes on until you are in the grave. In doing it you learn to subdue spirits in the house, and then you can come into the congregation as a leader and help other brothers and sisters do the same. Everything has a takeaway. Even when you hear somebody else being judged and corrected, it is about you, because at some point you will stand in that same position. Learn from what you observe, from what you hear, and from what the Lord shows us in ourselves, our families, the congregation and the nation.

“Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan; Only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war.” Why did the Lord leave those nations? To teach them war. The nations are the Lord’s sword, here to teach us how to war.

That doesn’t mean go get your Glock. If you have that thought process you are being simple. The Lord is teaching us something very important and always showing us something, and we should be ever learning.

sense.text:
We just read in Judges that the Lord left the nations to teach the next generation war, because they were not alive during the wars we are reading here. Each generation is being taught to war.

“Fear not, neither be thou dismayed: take all the people of war with thee, and arise, go up to Ai: see, I have given into thy hand the king of Ai, and his people, and his city, and his land.” Before they ever went there, the Lord said “I have given into thy hand.” The Lord had already determined the victory.

“Lay thee an ambush for the city behind it.” God says, I have already given you the city, but here is the war strategy I want you to use. Why didn’t the Lord just tell them to walk in and take it? Because he wanted to see whether they would be rebellious or follow his instructions. The Lord determined they would win, but they had to go about it his way.

We have already been preordained to gain the victory, but we must go about it the way the Lord has determined. Don’t reinvent anything. Don’t make up your own version. Do as the Lord commanded, and what he ordained will be yours. It is that simple.

Joshua chose out thirty thousand mighty men of valour and sent them by night: “ye shall lie in wait against the city, even behind the city: go not very far from the city, but be ye all ready.” Ambush it from behind, but don’t go too far, because the Lord ordained the war strategies and tactics, down to how far to go.

“When they come out against us, as at the first, that we will flee before them.” Joshua’s plan was to stand at the front of the city, draw the men of Ai out, and run. Think about those mighty men. They had been conquering nations since Moses passed the torch to Joshua; they had been on a winning streak and knew they could kill all those men. Now Joshua says, we are going to run. And they followed suit, because whatever he commanded them, they were going to do.

“Then ye shall rise up from the ambush, and seize upon the city: for the Lord your God will deliver it into your hand.” The Lord your God will deliver it. Then “ye shall set the city on fire: according to the commandment of the Lord shall ye do. See, I have commanded you.”

The ambush went and abode “between Beth–el and Ai, on the west side of Ai”: behind the city and to the west. Joshua and the people of war “pitched on the north side of Ai”, and about five thousand men were set to lie in ambush on the west side of the city. The host was on the north and the liers in wait on the west, just as the Lord gave it.

The king of Ai “and all his people” went out against Israel to battle, “but he wist not that there were liers in ambush against him behind the city.” He didn’t know the Lord had given Israel war tactics and strategies. He didn’t know men were waiting to take his city.

“Joshua and all Israel made as if they were beaten before them, and fled by the way of the wilderness.” The men of Ai thought they had the victory. Mighty Joshua, whom everyone had heard about for all his victories, was on the run, and they started feeling prideful: Israel beat all the neighbouring cities, but we are the ones chasing them. So “all the people that were in Ai were called together to pursue after them.”

“There was not a man left in Ai or Beth–el, that went not out after Israel: and they left the city open.” They had tunnel vision. All they could see was Israel fleeing into the wilderness. Every one of them forgot the city was left wide open, with no man to guard it or watch over it. Everybody wanted a part of a victory that our God had already ordained was going to Israel.

“Stretch out the spear that is in thy hand toward Ai; for I will give it into thine hand.” As soon as Joshua stretched out his hand, the ambush arose quickly, entered the city, took it, “and set the city on fire.”

“When the men of Ai looked behind them, they saw, and, behold, the smoke of the city ascended up to heaven, and they had no power to flee this way or that way.” Think how defeated they felt. You are cheering and chasing Israel, sure you have the victory, and the only thing that snaps you out of it is the smoke of your own home burning behind you. It’s a setup. They had no power to run back to their city to restock supplies or get more weapons. It was burning.

“And the people that fled to the wilderness turned back upon the pursuers.” All of a sudden Joshua and them stopped running. Think how the Lord lined it up perfectly: no alerts on their phones, and they all stopped at once and turned. You thought we were running for real?

“They turned again, and slew the men of Ai.” The men of Ai had nowhere to run, and Joshua and his men killed them all.

So the Lord taught his soldiers how to war and gave them war strategy. When we watch movies like Braveheart, with the hiding among villages and dressing up as soldiers, they are getting those tactics from the Bible, from our words. That is what the Lord commanded us to do to the nations. Now the nations put it in cinematography and we think it was their original idea. It is not. Our God gave us the tactics of war.

“Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature.” Christ is the image of the invisible God, because we have not been dealing with the Most High God: we have not seen his face nor his shape nor heard his voice. Christ is the firstborn of every creature. The Most High created Christ, and Christ created everything else.

“For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers.” Christ created the thrones, the powers and the principalities.

“All things were created by him, and for him”: to do his will, for his glory. The nations are his sword. They are doing the Lord’s bidding by whipping Israel back to repentance. The Lord put them in that position to beat us back to repentance.

precepts.why:
“To the intent that the living may know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will.” There is a kingdom of men as far as the eye can see, on every continent, in every country, town and village. But the Most High rules over it and gives it to whomsoever he will. Who that principality is, who sits on that throne, who that power is, is all determined by the Lord our God. Christ is like one playing a chess game, moving all the pieces into place for his will to be done.

“And setteth up over it the basest of men”: the lowest of the low. You have to be low down to do what these nations do to each other, and to do to the nation of Israel what they have done.

The Lord did it that way so we would learn war. If all the powers that be were the nicest people on earth, what war would you be in, and what tactics would you learn? Nothing. There would be no war on the earth and no oppression. But we transgressed against the Lord, so the Lord said, I have to teach you war, how to fight to get back to where you are supposed to be.

Some brothers and sisters don’t want to be in this fight. They send emails and messages saying they are taking a break. Taking a break from the Lord? That isn’t going to work.

sense.text:
“For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh.” We walk in the flesh, but the war we are actually fighting is not after the flesh. Our fore-parents of old warred after the flesh, as we read in Joshua and Judges, but there is a spiritual side to it all; there is a spirit in everything.

The war in Joshua was physical, but the spiritual side of it was obedience. In Joshua 6 and 7 they were disobedient with the Babylonish garment, and they lost and were put to death. The spiritual aspect of war is obedience to the Lord.

We don’t war after the flesh: it is not a carnal fight where you hurt someone or damage something and feel the victory. The Lord didn’t tell you to fight in that manner or give you those instructions. We want to fight our own way, and it isn’t going to work.

“Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God”: this part is very important for the rest of the class, every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God.

“And bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ.” Every thought, brought into captivity to the obedience of Christ.

precepts.why:
“For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers.” In Colossians 1 we just read who created the principalities and the powers: Christ. Paul is encouraging the church of Ephesus that there is a fight that has to happen, a war going on, and it is not a physical war between flesh and blood. It is a spiritual war.

Like a chess game: the black against the white, opposing players, both trying to win. Christ created the principalities and the powers, gave us the understanding of how to war, and said, now you have to war against those principalities and powers that I created, just as he created the nation of Israel. All things were made by him. He created opposing sides.

So this battle is not about flesh and blood. Don’t go try to buy a rocket launcher or a submarine with nuclear weapons. You will go to jail. It is not that kind of fight. The Lord ordained the fight in the flesh to be between the nations. Let them war in the flesh, not you.

“Against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.” It is as clear as day: we war against spiritual wickedness in high places.

The principalities the Lord created, those devils, gave us another gospel. They were warring against us and we didn’t even know it. You thought Christianity was the way back to God; that is why most of us went to church. You had been drinking for thirty-nine years and smoking crack in the eighties and wanted to get right with the Lord. So they put a church on every corner as the symbol of how to get back to the Lord, but the church pulls you further away from him.

sense.text:
“Who changed the truth of God into a lie.” Someone, somewhere, changed the truth of God into a lie. Paul is dealing with the Israelites in Rome, explaining that the Lord put things in place but they have been changed. And who were the powers that be at that time? Rome.

“And worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.” The truth of God was changed so much that the creature is served more than Christ himself, the Creator. Christ is blessed for ever.

“For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen.” Christ created all things, seen and unseen. You can’t see the air you breathe, but if the air supply is cut off, we all drop dead. Think how all the ecosystems work perfectly together. Evolution can’t do that. Big bang theories can’t do that. They are trying to figure out how God is God, so they give you all these theories to throw you off, just like they give you all the Christian churches to throw you off. It is all the same thing.

“Being understood by the things that are made”: we are the things that are made. By the perfect synchronization of everything, the bees and the flowers all working together, we should understand there must be a God. It is obvious. If evolution is true, why did the monkeys stop evolving? They should still be getting up out of the trees, opening the lock and walking out of the zoo. They stopped because God created them: Christ created them, and created man. These creatures are trying to find a way to disannul our God, and our God is too big for you to disannul. They taught us in school that we came from one single organism swimming in a lake, that crawled out, walked on the earth and lived in a cave, and once the Lord gave you back the Bible you saw that was dumb as hell. They thought we were the cavemen. We ain’t the damn cavemen. The white man’s the damn caveman.

“Even his eternal power and Godhead”: just by what we see and by past desolations, you should understand God’s eternal power. “So that they are without excuse”: what is obvious to us, the Bible says is obvious to everybody. There should be no atheists, no one worshipping Allah, nobody worshipping these other gods, because it is obvious the Creator made everything in its perfect form, and all for his will.

“Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not”. We knew God, and we did not glorify him. That goes right back to obedience. We knew what God required of us and what his instructions are, and we don’t glorify the Lord when we start doing our own thing, being self-willed, making up our own ways.

“Neither were thankful”: we were not thankful for all the Lord provided. “But became vain in their imaginations”: our thought processes became unprofitable. “And their foolish heart was darkened”: our minds were darkened.

“Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools.” Everything that proves there is a God is right in front of us; all the creation is too big for there not to be a God. Yet we were unthankful, did not glorify him, had vain imaginations and foolishness, and still professed ourselves to be wise. We are some deep dummies.

“And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.” We didn’t glorify the Lord, and we thought ourselves so wise that we changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like corruptible man.

precepts.why:
“But that which is made with hands is cursed, as well it, as he that made it: he, because he made it; and it, because, being corruptible, it was called god.”

This is the war of the gods. Early in the class we read that our God is God alone, all power, creating light and darkness, creating peace and evil. The Lord does all these things; he teaches us war strategies; he made the principalities and the powers. But we didn’t glorify him. We went after vain imaginations and professed ourselves to be wise, and so we made idolatrous images after the image of corruptible man, and then we called them God. The thing made with hands is cursed, and so is the one who made it.

sense.text:
“Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?” We just read that the things we form after corruptible man are cursed, and the maker is cursed too. Now this is Christ: Christ is also a maker. He made everything seen and unseen, in earth and in heaven.

Do the things he formed turn back to him and ask why he made them that way? It is a rhetorical question, because everything he made is in its perfect form and perfect order. The hummingbirds don’t stop getting nectar from the plants in your yard. Lions don’t stop chasing the beasts. The mothers still give suck to their young, as it says in Lamentations. The whales don’t decide to get out and walk on land. The water does not pass the bounds of the sand unless a storm is involved, and a storm happens because the Lord is visiting the earth, sending his angels down in those storms to stir things up; only by his directive does the water move contrary. As Ecclesiastes 1 says, the rain comes down, fills the lakes and the ocean, evaporates to the clouds and comes back down again. Perfect order.

The only thing out of order in the world is us. Everything is in perfect order except the twelve tribes of Israel. The Lord says, Israel, keep my commandments that you may live, and we say, we ain’t doing that. But the Lord is teaching us something. War is coming whether you stay in basic training or not.

“Hath not the potter power over the clay”: doesn’t Christ have power over all of us that he made? “Of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour.” Like the chessboard: on one side vessels of honour, on the other vessels of dishonour, and Christ created both.

From the same lump: Jacob and Esau came from the same mother and father. One is the vessel unto honour, Jacob, whom we descend from, and the other is the vessel unto dishonour. That is what it is really about.

“What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction.” While the nations fulfil their role as God’s sword, he endures them with much longsuffering and lets them do what he created them for. And what were they created for? Destruction. They are here to serve a purpose, and then the Lord is going to destroy them. Some of you look like a tear just fell. Wipe your tears. The nations got to go.

“For a father afflicted with untimely mourning, when he hath made an image of his child soon taken away, now honoured him as a god, which was then a dead man.” We made things and called them god, and now the nations do the same thing: they made an image in the likeness of a son and honoured it as a god. Look at the bust of the saviour, posed for by Caesar Borgia: that is the image the world honours as a god.

“Thus in process of time”: we just read that the Lord is longsuffering with the vessels fitted to destruction. Over a process of time the son of perdition must be revealed, the devil on earth must be revealed. The Lord is saying, do what I created you to do. He created the principalities and the powers, and he sits back. But what he is really watching is what we, the children of Israel, are going to do.

“An ungodly custom grown strong was kept as a law, and graven images were worshipped by the commandments of kings.” Worshipping Caesar Borgia as a god became a custom, then turned into a law; the kings gave commandments to worship graven images. Now the children of Israel do it willingly.

So there is a war of the gods. One poured out all his goodness upon us. We forsook him, rejected his glory, and began to worship idols and other gods, first by force, now willingly. Ask somebody today if we are in slavery and they say, no, we’ve been free. No. You are still in chains; they are just wrapped around your head, around your mind.

“They took the counterfeit of his visage from far, and made an express image of a king whom they honoured.” It is not really him; it is a counterfeit replica of his image. It used to be a staple to have the big Jesus piece: the first thing a Negro did with his tax money was get the chain with Jesus on it, with Caesar on it, with a little ice on it too. It was a way to deceive us even further. Get that damn idol out of your house. Don’t keep it thinking you’ll pawn it or melt it down one day.

“To the end that by this their forwardness they might flatter him that was absent, as if he were present.”

“Also the singular diligence of the artificer did help to set forward the ignorant to more superstition.” The artificer is the sculptor who made the image. He added superstition to it: not only the image, but a story behind it. That is what is called marketing today. They don’t just give you a Red Bull; they tell you it gives you wings. It is the same with the Christmas tree: the storyline that came with it, and the Krampus and Black Pete that came along with it. We are reading about that out of the Bible.

“For he, peradventure willing to please one in authority, forced all his skill to make the resemblance of the best fashion.” He used every bit of his skill to make it in the best resemblance of that dead son, Caesar Borgia. And the storyline that came with it was: this is God, this is the Messiah, this is he who resurrected, and if you don’t bow down and worship him you won’t gain salvation.

That is the storyline of John 3:16 as they gave it: all nations can be saved in this image. Yet in the fourteenth, fifteenth, sixteenth, seventeenth, eighteenth and even nineteenth centuries that storyline didn’t apply to us. We didn’t gain salvation; we were beaten behind it.

“And so the multitude, allured by the grace of the work, took him now for a god.” Behind the marketing pitch, behind the threats and scares of what Jesus will do, none of it out of the Bible, the multitude was allured. He used the best colours, made the cheeks rosy and the eyes the bluest of blue, and they believed the pitch and took him for a god. But he was nothing more than a dead man, a dead devil that never rose again: “which a little before was but honoured.”

“And this was an occasion to deceive the world”: this is the labour they put forth to deceive the entire world.

“For men, serving either calamity or tyranny, did ascribe unto stones and stocks the incommunicable name.” Because of all the labour that went into falsifying the Messiah, many started to put that name onto stocks and stones: the holy water you can buy from Peter Popoff at two in the morning, the holy rags and handkerchiefs, the miracle spring water that is dirty tap water. All of it sold by associating it with Jesus.

“Moreover this was not enough for them, that they erred in the knowledge of God”: adding the incommunicable name to stones and stocks and deceiving the world was not enough; they went further.

“But whereas they lived in the great war of ignorance.” There is an ever-going war whether you like it or not, and here it is called the great war of ignorance. It is still a deprogramming: when you hear the name Jesus, your mind automatically goes to Caesar, and it takes time to get that out of your mind. Some of you saw that Jesus piece and were mesmerized, remembering the club back in ’93. That was glorified among our people.

We subscribed to things like come as you are, Jesus takes me as I am, meaning you don’t have to change. But the Bible is all about change. In Joshua they were accustomed to warring a certain way, then the Lord told them to set ambushes to the north and the west. We can’t stay stuck in the old mode, still on AOL dial-up when it has moved on to AI. Many brothers and sisters have grown in their war strategies, because the Lord has given them skills to help push this fight.

“Those so great plagues called they peace.” They call the great war of ignorance peace.

precepts.why:
This is how you remove yourself from the great war of ignorance: “But he that giveth his mind to the law of the most High, and is occupied in the meditation thereof, will seek out the wisdom of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.”

We wrestle against the great war of ignorance, and the Bible tells us how to get out of it. We have to purge certain terms and certain imagery from our minds by giving ourselves over to the laws of God and being occupied in the meditation thereof.

Seek out the wisdom of the ancients: those of old, all the prophets and the apostles, and also our ancients among us now, our Bishops and our Deacons. Seek out their wisdom. How do I become a better leader? How do I build my household? How do I teach my son and my daughter? What steps did you take? Those who have been in the truth thirty-five or forty years can help all of us who have been in it two or three years. There is a lot we can learn, but we don’t seek out the wisdom of those who gave themselves over to the laws of God. We need to, and we must.

sense.text: We just read that we must be occupied in prophecies, and this is a prophecy, a time to come. “Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom; We have heard a rumour from the Lord, and an ambassador is sent among the heathen, Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle.”
“Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.” The prophecy concerning Edom is that they will be greatly despised.

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”: they are so prideful that they themselves are deceived.

“Thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock”: they are the damn cavemen. That’s them. Karen has the nerve to come out and tell you don’t park there, you don’t belong here, being black in Starbucks, and you were in a cave cutting up juniper roots. Their pride has deceived them so that they think they are the wise of the earth and the most civilized of the earth. No: they are the most demonic of the earth.

“Whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” They are so prideful they ask this question as though they are God.

“Say unto the prince of Tyrus”: we are reading the prophecy of Edom, and Edom was also called Tyrus. In Ezekiel 28 he is talking about Edom.

“Because thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas.” They sit in the midst of the seas: all their bases around the world. “Yet thou art a man, and not God”: Ezekiel tells Edom, who thinks he is God, you are just a regular man. “Though thou set thine heart as the heart of God”: though you set your mind as the mind of God, you are not God.

“Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel.” Through all their technological advances they are wiser than Daniel: they can listen through your smart TV and your phone. “There is no secret that they can hide from thee”: you think it is a charging block, and they have charging blocks now with cameras in them.

“With thy wisdom and with thine understanding thou hast gotten thee riches, and hast gotten gold and silver into thy treasures: By thy great wisdom and by thy traffick hast thou increased thy riches, and thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches.” Through their wisdom they have gotten riches, and their heart is lifted up because of them.
“Because thou hast set thine heart as the heart of God; Behold, therefore I will bring strangers upon thee.” The strangers the Lord brings upon them are the nations.
“Tubal–cain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”: Tubal-cain designed weaponry.

“I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt. If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.” That lineage, which comes through Cain, eventually comes back to be Esau, and they were given the art of weaponry. So much so that Lamech says, if anybody tries to avenge, I am raining hellfire on whoever it was.

precepts.why:
Isaac to Esau: “Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above; And by thy sword shalt thou live.” By your weaponry you will live.

“And shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.” Esau would serve his brother, but his ability with the sword would be so great that he would break the yoke his brother had over him.

And the principalities, the powers and the thrones were all created by Christ.

“Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work.” Who created Cain and Lamech? Who created Esau? Christ did. He gave them the ability to have dominion, power, principalities, spiritual wickedness in high places.

The smith that brings forth an instrument for his work is what we saw in Genesis 4 with Tubal-cain. And as we are occupied in prophecies, Isaiah is prophesying of the smith in those days and in the days to come.

“And I have created the waster to destroy.” There is the smith, Tubal-cain, Cain and Lamech, and then there is the waster. An arrow, a dart, a knife or a sword does not destroy on its own; the waster is created to destroy.

sense.text:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning!” Here is another name for Esau. We saw Tyrus, we saw Edom, and now Lucifer. “How art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” How did he weaken the nations? Through war. But he is going to fall, as we read in Obadiah, because his pride has reached up unto heaven.

Two fighter jets fired missiles at a United States Navy warship, and within ninety-three seconds both aircraft were falling debris across three miles of ocean, and the destroyer hadn’t even changed course. Before those jets reached cruising altitude, the system had calculated seventeen ways to kill them. That is why the pride of this man is lifted up.

“Thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon.” In verse 12 he is called Lucifer; further up in the chapter he is called the king of Babylon. “How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” He was going to be taken down. How did you fall, being such a great, magnificent city and people, supposedly?

“He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke.” We just saw Venezuela: the weapons defence system taken down, the bases bombed, the president extracted from an entire country with a military before anyone knew he was gone, before he got out of bed into his bunker, all in thirty minutes. It takes you longer to cook dinner. And remember the great war of ignorance: people see these things and say he must be God, or God must be with them.

“He that ruled the nations in anger, is persecuted, and none hindereth.” He smote the people with a continual stroke, primarily God’s people, but he weakens all the nations.
“The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet: they break forth into singing.” When he falls, when these devils fall, the whole earth will finally be at rest.

“I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.” They are so deceived that, with all the military might they have had since the time of Tubal-cain, they feel like they are like the Most High, or the actual Most High.

The US Space Command headquarters is moving to Huntsville, Alabama, and they said from this day forward it would be known as Rocket City. That means a lot of weaponry. Remember, Christ said he created the smith and the waster.

precepts.why: Back to Obadiah: “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee.” They are deceived. We read it earlier, and we have to go back there, because that deceiving pride is what speaks in Isaiah 14:14, “I will be like the most High.” It is the same one who says in his heart, “Who shall bring me down to the ground?”

“And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms.” He called Huntsville, Alabama a beautiful place; Babylon is the glory of kingdoms. All these nations want to come to Babylon and get a piece of it. They call it the American dream: we just want a piece of the American dream.

sense.text: “And I saw one of his heads as it were wounded to death; and his deadly wound was healed: and all the world wondered after the beast.” All the world was amazed at the beast.

“And they worshipped the dragon which gave power unto the beast”: the devil himself gives power to the beast, and the beast is the white man.

“And they worshipped the beast, saying, Who is like unto the beast? who is able to make war with him?” Who is like the beast, who was created for the perfection of warfare? Who can make war with him?

DARPA, the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, is the most powerful portion of Esau’s military. It likes the public perception that it does all these things for the good of humanity, but the secretary of defense who went to Congress for its funding said it was going to create the vast weapon systems of the future. They are always twenty years ahead of anything you or I know; whatever military weapon you see now, DARPA has the version twenty years more advanced. That is why our war is not according to flesh and blood.

The soldiers in Venezuela said they started gushing blood out of their nose and mouth and couldn’t control their bowels, and everybody is amazed. But they did the same thing in the eighties in Panama: the Bishop has told us a million times to watch The Panama Deception, where people said there were lasers and people disintegrating. They laid down an entire army, bleeding and helpless, without firing one bullet.

They changed the name of the Department of War to the Department of Defense after World War II, and they say they haven’t won a major war since, so they went back to the Department of War. Words matter. They understand how important a name is, just as we should all understand how important the name of Israel is, not Jenkins, Johnson, Rodriguez, Mendoza or Franklin.

precepts.why:
“Therefore hear now this, thou that art given to pleasures, that dwellest carelessly”: this place is given to pleasures and dwells carelessly, as though no one can take it down. “That sayest in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me; I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children”: no one can cause them to lose lives.

“For thou hast trusted in thy wickedness: thou hast said, None seeth me.” They trust in their wickedness. “Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee; and thou hast said in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me.” That is the pride of the beast of whom they say, “Who is like unto the beast?”

“Because thou hast set thine heart as the heart of God; Behold, therefore I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations.” The world asks who is able to make war with the beast, and the Lord answers: the terrible of the nations shall come upon them.

sense.text:
“And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb.” Here is the great war of ignorance. Look at the numbers of the children of Israel throughout the four corners of the earth: most of them worship the white man. They can’t see a kingdom of people that look like them. In Nigeria, Sierra Leone or Liberia they are in a huge congregation where everybody looks like them, and with one consent they all worship the white man. The Bishops and Deacons went to Papua New Guinea: dark people, all of them worshipping Caesar Borgia. That is what we have been reading all day.

Some of you have taught your mothers, fathers, brothers and sisters, and after all the scriptures and all the time you spent, they say, yeah, I see you learned the Bible, but I’m going to keep on worshipping this white man. That is what it boils down to.

precepts.why:
Here is something else the Lord calls Edom in this context: “Now the Egyptians are men, and not God.” The Lord has to reaffirm that they are men and not God, because there is a video depicting Donald Trump as a messiah-like figure, as God.

Don’t think their weaponry is only for warring with other people. It is to force a thought into our minds, to force white supremacy into our spirits. So there is a war of gods: the God you still have in your mind and the God of this Bible. And the war is in your mind, in ignorance.

He doesn’t look like Caesar Borgia, but spiritually he sees a Borgia. Brad Pitt, Tom Cruise, Bill Gates, all of them see a Borgia, because they are all about white supremacy, and that is what Caesar Borgia is about.

sense.text: “And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.” There is going to be civil war. The Lord is teaching us war tactics because there are going to be wars in the flesh, and we have to stay strong in the war we have in our spirit.

“And the spirit of Egypt shall fail in the midst thereof; and I will destroy the counsel thereof: and they shall seek to the idols, and to the charmers, and to them that have familiar spirits, and to the wizards.” As the Lord brings destruction through civil war and external wars, they are going to seek to the images they revered as gods. They will talk to those Jesus pieces: come save us, we are going through hell. They will seek out the news outlets that have been lying to us for years, seek out Christianity, all the different versions of white supremacy, in that day.

“The Lord hath mingled a perverse spirit in the midst thereof: and they have caused Egypt to err in every work thereof.” God put a perverse spirit in this place, and it causes it to err in every work. Everything America does is in error, because there is a perverse spirit here.

When Trump went to the Ford plant, a worker called him a pedophile protector and he shot him the bird, and the man was suspended while the union fights for him. Somebody called out the perverse spirit, and even when they are shown their errors, the answer is to flip you the bird and make sure you lose your job.

precepts.why: So everybody knows where Egypt is: “And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt.” This place spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt. That is why there is a perverse spirit here.

sense.text: “Thou didst march through the land in indignation, thou didst thresh the heathen in anger.” Christ marched through the land in fury and threshed the heathen.
“Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people, even for salvation with thine anointed.” What is Christ bringing judgment for? For the salvation of his people, for our salvation.

“When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself, that I might rest in the day of trouble.” When the Lord revealed these things to Habakkuk his belly trembled. He prays that he might be at rest in that day, because it is going to be a terrible time.

“When he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops.” Another word for troops is soldiers. We read about us being soldiers of old, and here Christ is coming back with his army, with a legion of angels, to invade them with his troops.

precepts.why: “Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.” The Lord will take vengeance, and when Christ comes back with his troops he is not coming back as a regular man that you can do any harm to.

sense.text: “But the righteous live for evermore”: the righteous are going to live for evermore. “Their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High.”

“Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the Lord’s hand.” The Lord himself is going to place that crown upon you. “For with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.”
“He shall take to him his jealousy for complete armour, and make the creature his weapon for the revenge of his enemies.” The creature shall be the weapon for the revenge of his enemies.

“And one shall undertake to fight against another, one city against another, one place against another, one people against another, and one realm against another.” There will be wars one against another, city against city, as we read earlier in Isaiah 19.
“And then shall my Son be declared, whom thou sawest as a man ascending.” Then shall Christ be declared.
“And this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations, which for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest.” Christ shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations.

“And shall lay before them their evil thoughts, and the torments wherewith they shall begin to be tormented, which are like unto a flame: and he shall destroy them without labour by the law.” Their torments are like a flame, a fire, and he shall destroy them without labour.
